Introduction

Missouri Home Care Providers offer Personal Care and Chore Services to individuals in their homes. The MO Department of Health & Senior Services — Bureau of Home Care & Rehabilitative Standards oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Missouri’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Missouri’s Regulations

The Bureau of Home Care & Rehabilitative Standards licenses home care providers. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, chore services, homemaker services, and companion care.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the MO Secretary of State, apply for provider license, secure insurance, and enroll as Medicaid provider if applicable.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Missouri benchmarks: Private pay rates $18-$26/hour, Medicaid rates $14-$20/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling systems, and quality monitoring tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Missouri requires background checks and training for all direct care staff.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop comprehensive operational policies per state requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build referral networks in Kansas City, St. Louis, and outstate communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and ongoing compliance requirements.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between personal care and chore services? Personal care involves direct assistance with ADLs; chore services include housekeeping and errands.
